trust_decision.summary: Secret X25519/X448 scalar (dA) must not drive data-dependent branches/timing: the PHP field add/subtract branch on the result value, and Montgomery private-key loaders derive QA with the pure-PHP ladder instead of delegating to libsodium/OpenSSL.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'X25519 scalar multiplication'; the Montgomery ladder multiplyPoint (branch on scalar bit at line 230) is the obvious first place, reached via Curve25519::multiplyPoint (phpseclib/Crypt/EC/Curves/Curve25519.php:50-64).

fix_sites.entry_point: PrimeField\Integer::add() (public Math API), reached by every Montgomery ladder step (phpseclib/Crypt/EC/BaseCurves/Montgomery.php:186-201)
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level math library (Math package, separate from Crypt\EC)

fix_sites.entry_point: PrimeField\Integer::subtract() (public Math API), same ladder steps
PrimeField\Integer::setModulo() / cleanupCache() at 120-127 (mask cache setup, fix.diff:148-163)
EC::load / PublicKeyLoader::load of PKCS8 id-X25519/id-X448 private key without embedded public key
new shared helper deriveMontgomeryPublicKey (fix.diff:28-74) used by both loaders; honours EC::forceEngine (phpseclib/Crypt/Common/AsymmetricKey.php:441-461)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: phpseclib/Math/PrimeField/Integer.php:183-212 (generic prime-field add/subtract shared with Prime/Koblitz/Edwards curves, a different package from Crypt\EC)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: PrimeField\Integer is a generic arithmetic class used by all curves and BigInteger itself is variable-time, so a solver can argue constant-time field ops are a library-wide redesign outside an X25519 report, and that the PHP ladder is only a fallback once libsodium/OpenSSL are used.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: EC::forceEngine('PHP') must still compute X25519/X448 in pure PHP and Curve448 must keep working without libsodium (libsodium only supports Curve25519); public keys must still match RFC 7748 results; forcing OpenSSL for PrivateKey::multiply throws by design. An over-broad fix that hard-requires libsodium/OpenSSL or rejects Curve448 breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: PKCS8 id-X25519 private key without publicKey field
PKCS8 id-X448 private key without publicKey field
engine selection variants: none forced / libsodium forced / OpenSSL forced / PHP forced (fix.diff:32-73)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ECDH shared-secret computation PrivateKey::multiply uses the PHP ladder for Curve448, for Curve25519 without ext-sodium, and under forceEngine('PHP'); the fix does not delegate or harden the ladder's per-bit branch
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fix only touched key loading; multiply already prefers libsodium for Curve25519 and OpenSSL is explicitly unsupported there, so the PHP path looks like an accepted fallback
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (Crypt/EC/PrivateKey.php) from the Formats/Keys loaders; same EC package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DH::computeSecret falls through to PrivateKey::multiply when openssl_pkey_derive is missing or fails
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A different class (DH) and an OpenSSL-failure fallback path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: EC::createKey pure-PHP fallback derives QA with the PHP ladder (Curve448 before PHP 8.4 OPENSSL_KEYTYPE_X448, Curve25519 without sodium/OpenSSL, or forced PHP)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Key generation path, not 'loading'; the new helper is private to the Formats trait and the fallback only runs when no engine exists
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (Crypt/EC.php) from the Formats/Keys loaders

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Montgomery ladder itself still selects the branch on each secret scalar bit, with no constant-time conditional swap
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Both branches call doubleAndAddPoint with swapped arguments, so it can be argued to be balanced already
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: BaseCurves package, the landing point itself

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SSH2 curve25519-sha256 KEX reaches the createKey and computeSecret fallbacks above
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Transport layer in Net\, far from Crypt\EC; only a caller
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (Net) and a very large file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a loader for a key with an embedded publicKey whose QA is recomputed or validated against dA via the PHP ladder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers often add 'verify public matches private' checks during load, and that check would reuse multiplyPoint

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getPublicKey/toString re-deriving QA from dA for Montgomery curves instead of using the stored QA
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A save/reload path that recomputes the public key on export is a common convenience refactor

O8b_injection_room.sibling: negate()/a conditional-reduce helper that keeps a value-dependent branch like the old add/subtract
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same class, same idiom; a maintainer fixing add/subtract could plausibly miss a third reduction helper

O9_family: timing side channel (CWE-208/CWE-385) in secret-scalar elliptic-curve arithmetic

O10_build.toolchain: PHP + composer + phpunit; optional ext-sodium and ext-openssl (PHP 8.4 for X25519/X448 OpenSSL keytypes)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Unit/Crypt/EC/CurveTest.php, tests/Unit/Crypt/EC/KeyTest.php (the fix diff adds no tests)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Rewrite the Montgomery ladder with a constant-time cswap in BaseCurves/Montgomery.php, or add a libsodium shortcut in Curve25519::multiplyPoint, leaving the PrimeField add/subtract branches and the Curve448/PKCS8 loader paths untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: PrimeField\Integer::multiply/divide (modInverse) and BigInteger reductions are also variable-time (phpseclib/Math/PrimeField/Integer.php:219-237); they are library-wide and the published fix leaves them alone.
Edwards/Prime-curve signing paths (phpseclib/Crypt/EC/PrivateKey.php:196, 250, 277) use the same field class but are a different protection (ECDSA/EdDSA).
unverified: Testability: the property is timing; hidden tests would have to be structural or engine-routing (for example forced-engine behaviour, branchless add/subtract results at the boundaries, QA equality across engines), not measured timing. This is not on the red-flag list but is the main risk for this host.
